articles.headline: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh on struggling Justin Herbert: 'Be better'
articles.description: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh offered a rare public critique of Justin Herbert on Monday, imploring the quarterback to "be better."
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh offered a rare public critique of quarterback Justin Herbert a day after the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

​"Be better. Be better," Harbaugh said of Herbert's decision-making. "And that drives Justin, that drives me, that drives his position coach, that drives Mike [McDaniel], the coordinator. I mean, drives us all."

Since he took the job in 2023, Harbaugh has avoided criticizing his star quarterback, often willing to point out other players' mistakes in defense of Herbert. Harbaugh said Herbert's interception in Week 2 against the Las Vegas Raiders was wide receiver Derius Davis' fault, for example. In Week 1, when two Arizona Cardinals defenders ran free at Herbert for a sack, Harbaugh said Herbert's protection calls weren't an issue; rather, wide receiver Tre' Harris ran the wrong route.

Harbaugh has said throughout his tenure that he thinks Herbert is the greatest quarterback of all time. He once said he wishes he could trade genes with Herbert because of how perfect a player and person he is.

​Last week, Harbaugh said he "wouldn't change a thing about Justin."

​That makes Harbaugh's criticisms Monday all the more meaningful, as Herbert hasn't looked like the player many consider among the NFL's most talented quarterbacks this season.

​Sunday's game marked another poor performance for Herbert, who looks like a shell of himself in offensive coordinator McDaniel's offense. Herbert finished with 226 passing yards, one touchdown and an interception, but could have easily had three picks if Bills defenders hadn't dropped two. ​The interception that was caught, by Bills' safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, was almost thrown directly to the safety. The ball was intended for wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling, but Gardner-Johnson was in coverage, clearly waiting for the ball.

​"Poor awareness, poor decision. Throws him a meatball sub," said Tom Brady, the former quarterback turned color commentator for Fox Sports.

​The offense has been the Chargers' Achilles' heel through three games. General manager Joe Hortiz spent this offseason retooling the offense in McDaniel's vision, a scheme based on anticipatory throwing and wide zone runs. In training camp, McDaniel said Herbert had been significantly ahead of any other quarterbacks he had worked with in their first year in the system, but Herbert has never looked less comfortable through three games.

​The Chargers lost despite the defense forcing five turnovers Sunday, when the offense scored only 14 points. Time and time again, the defense gave the offense an opportunity as the Chargers searched for their first win of the season.

Instead, Herbert and the offense looked as disjointed as they had all year -- drops from tight end Oronde Gadsden and Quentin Johnston, five offensive penalties in the third quarter, and even a missed Cameron Dicker field goal attempt.

articles.headline: Zion Williamson, on cusp of 8th season, not where he wants to be
articles.description: Zion Williamson smiled politely, but kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player, saying "I'm not where I need to be."
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- Zion Williamson smiled politely, but kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player.

"I'm not where I want to be," Williamson said, nodding in apparent acknowledgement of how little the New Orleans Pelicans have accomplished since drafting the magnetic power forward first overall out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be."

For the eighth time on Monday, the 26-year-old Williamson donned a Pelicans uniform for the franchise's media day. If he's still wearing a jersey when the playoffs start in mid April, it will be a first in his highly lucrative, yet largely unsatisfying NBA career.

Williamson's new coach Jamahl Mosley will be his fifth.

"It's not the way I would have wanted it to be, but that's just part of this business," Williamson said. "All you can do is just adjust with it and hope that things get better."

Williamson has missed 278 career games -- including the entire 2021-22 season -- because of a series of injuries and struggles with fitness. But when he has played, he has averaged nearly 24 points, mixing his uncanny ability to finish through contact in the paint with explosive, above-the-rim highlights.

Now Williamson appears committed, perhaps like never before, to do his part to improve the Pelicans' fortunes. He has reported for training camp in "impeccable condition," according Pelicans basketball operations chief Joe Dumars.

The 6-foot-6 Williamson is listed at 277 pounds, down from 284 -- a figure that had appeared on the club's official roster for the previous seven seasons.

"At some point, you just want the player to get it," said Dumars, now entering his second season with New Orleans. "If someone has to call you every morning to drag you out of bed, to get you to work out, you don't get it yet. But when you're up and you're doing it, and you're the one leading it, then you start looking at that guy and you go, 'Okay, he's good.'

"That's what I saw from him this year," Dumars continued. "You can't play 82 games and not be in great shape. And so we talked about him being in impeccable condition and he has done that."

Dumars said he also spoke with Williamson about becoming more of a leader and diversifying his game, namely by becoming a more consistent and willing jump shooter so that he can punish teams who defend him by collapsing into the paint.

Williamson spent the summer "working with different people, looking at the game different ways, just trying to find different ways to get better," he said. "I've improved with mentally trusting myself and trusting my game, just trusting the work I've put in to the point to where I'm not second-guessing myself."

Williamson summarized his new attitude toward shooting jump shots as: "If I miss, I miss. The next shot's going in."

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

"I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly."

Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon.

It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process.

A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule.

"My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. articles.headline: 76ers say 'sacrifice' key to success after offseason additions
articles.description: The 76ers say they are comfortable with making sacrifices for the benefit of the team after adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown in the offseason.
articles.headlineJa: オフの補強を経て、76ersは成功の鍵を「犠牲」と語る
articles.descriptionJa: オフシーズンにレブロン・ジェームズとジェイレン・ブラウンを加えた76ersは、チームの勝利のために犠牲を払う覚悟ができていると述べた。
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- With LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey officially coming together as Philadelphia 76ers teammates during the team's annual media day Monday, Brown was asked how the star-studded group would determine the "alpha" among them.

"Next question," Brown, the 2024 NBA Finals MVP acquired in an offseason trade with the Boston Celtics, replied.

Just because Brown chose to sidestep the question doesn't mean the main stars on the league's latest superteam don't know how much interest their every move will generate.

"You got to try to stay even keel," James said. "Understand that the noise is going to be the noise. What happens outside of this building is going to consistently happen and it's going to be doubled and tripled and quadrupled now that I'm here. It just comes with the territory. I understand it."

James, 41, entering an unprecedented 24th season, said the only way to outrun the scrutiny is to outwork it.

"The work that we put in in this building, the work that we put in when we're on the road, watching film, the work that we put in will take care of itself," James said. "Guys will hold each other accountable.

"Everything that's going on out there does not matter. It does not matter at all. It's about the results and the things that happen in this building for us."

To that end, James, Brown, Embiid and Maxey got on the court together for a workout at the Sixers training complex Monday prior to their media day obligations, Philadelphia sources told ESPN, to get a head start on the journey ahead. Even though training camp doesn't open until Tuesday.

"Going into this year, we just want to get as much time as possible with each other on and off the court, try to create those relationships, which we already have," said Embiid, the 2023 league MVP and a member of the Team USA gold medal group at the 2024 Paris Olympics along with James. "And then build from there. Every single day, wins and losses, learn something and keep evolving. Obviously, everyone has the same goal, and we've got to find a way to accomplish it. Day by day, keep getting better."

As the new group figures out the best way to win together, players will surely be asked to do things differently than they have in the past.

Maxey, an All-Star in two of the past three seasons and coming off a campaign in which he averaged a career-best 28.3 points (No. 5 in the league), said he welcomes the changes.

That will be a valuable attitude when trying to incorporate Brown, who was No. 4 in the league with 28.7 points per game. Not to mention the NBA's all-time leading scorer in James.

"I'm pretty comfortable playing in any type of situation at this point in my career," Maxey said. "I've kind of played under so many different circumstances.

articles.headline: Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) to make Eagles debut on Monday
articles.description: Edge Jonathan Greenard is set to make his Eagles debut Monday night. He has been sidelines with a pectoral injury he sustained while lifting weights over the summer.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Edge rusher Jonathan Greenard was active for Monday night's game at the Chicago Bears and will make his Philadelphia Eagles debut.

Greenard has been sidelined with a pectoral injury he sustained while lifting weights over the summer. He was listed as questionable on the injury report this week.

While the Eagles will gladly welcome Greenard into the mix, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said last Tuesday that he is "nowhere near ready" for a full workload.

"He's not only coming off inactivity, he's coming off an injury," Fangio said. "His injury for a good bit -- the first, I don't know, four to six, seven weeks -- he really couldn't do a whole lot conditioning-wise either."

Greenard was sidelined for all of training camp and for the first two regular-season games. The Eagles' defense has produced a 45% pressure rate through two games this season, the second-best rate entering Week 3 after the Vikings (48%), but has netted just three sacks, tied for the fifth fewest in the NFL.

Philadelphia acquired Greenard, 29, in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings during draft weekend in April and agreed to a lucrative new deal with the star linebacker.

The Eagles sent two third-round draft picks -- the No. 98 pick in this year's draft and a third-rounder next year -- to the Vikings for Greenard, who then agreed to a four-year, $100 million extension that also includes $50 million in guaranteed money.

Greenard is expected to assume a starting role for the Super Bowl-hopeful Eagles when healthy, leading a group that also includes Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, AJ Epenesa and Arnold Ebiketie.

Greenard had three sacks in 12 games last season after double-digit sack campaigns the previous two years in Minnesota.

He spent the first four years of his career with the Houston Texans before signing a four-year, $72 million deal with the Vikings in 2024. He recorded 12.5 sacks and was named to the Pro Bowl in his first season with the Vikings but was slowed because of a shoulder injury that ultimately required season-ending surgery in 2025.

articles.headline: NFL Week 3's best arrivals, led by Jalen Hurts
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.body:
The official start of fall means it's fit season, when players start dominating the gameday tunnels with eye-popping jackets, sweaters and pants.

Last week, the Philadelphia Eagles played a blazing hot game in Nashville that had players' cleats melting with with temperatures of up to 157 degrees Fahrenheit on the turf. 

Hopefully this week is the start of a heat decline with more cloudier 50-to-75 degree days ahead to allow players to comfortably show off their fits.

To kick off Week 3, Green Bay Packers quarterbacks Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor rocked my two favorite outfits of the Thursday primetime slate.

Love came in shining -- literally -- with a Public School New York x KAY jewelry collaboration jacket: the definition of a statement piece.

Meanwhile, Taylor's Dries Van Noten sweater is the perfect kickoff to fall -- warm but fashion-forward. There are so many fabric design details within this one piece, showing the value of layers.

Here are Week 3 fits that caught our eye:

Monday night fashion

The Philadelphia Eagles and Chicago Bears brought plenty of style to Soldier Field ahead of their "Monday Night Football" matchup. 

Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts pulled off a beige double-breasted suit look that was equal parts fly city jazz singer and CEO of an upstart-turned-Fortune 500 company.

This Week 3 fit is a perfect example of Hurts' signature soulful style that commands respect and translates seamlessly from the tunnel to the field to his postgame presser one-liners.

Sunday's best

For primetime show, it's a who wore it better. The Los Angeles Rams duo of Davante Adams and Byron Young went with all-denim jacket and pant combos. Both can't miss ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys brought their contrasting styles to Maracanã Stadium for the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro. Lamar Jackson donned a graphic tee paying homage to the late rapper DMX, while George Pickens' fit featured Brazil's national colors in a nod to the host country. 

San Francisco 49ers safety Malik Mustapha styling with an eye-popping Kid Super jacket was my favorite of this window.

From Stefon Diggs' black jacket covered in NBA throwback logo patches, to Malik Nabers' custom "H1M" pendant, players brought plenty of style and personality ahead of the early slate.

Four standouts in this window included Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson 's Boardwalk Vintage fit, which completed a preppy rockstar vibe. Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young KITH x New York to the world jersey was a winner. Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins leaned into the Fall Cleveland vibes with this unique Celine sweater. I love retro call backs so must give Diggs love on his vintage NBA bomber jacket.

Thursday night fashion

The Green Bay Packers host the Atlanta Falcons to kick off Week 3's slate, and quarterback Jordan Love entered the home opener in style, pairing an oversize studded leather pullover with black trousers

articles.headline: Wizards' Anthony Davis to wait until summer for extension talks
articles.description: Anthony Davis plans on finishing the season with the Washington Wizards before deciding on any potential contract extension, he said Monday.
articles.body:
Anthony Davis plans on finishing the season with the Washington Wizards before deciding on any potential contract extension, he said at Wizards media day on Monday.

Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania last month that the Wizards and Davis' agent, Rich Paul, mutually decided to wait on talks for an extension until the season began. One source told Charania at the time that it would give both sides the first 20 or so games to marinate over a potential deal and assess how the season goes.

Davis indicated a longer timeline when discussing how he would decide on remaining a Wizards after this season.

"[I'll decide] when the season is over. We're going to go through the season and try to do what I do at a high level," he said. "And then when it's over, sit down and have those conversations again with front office."

Davis became eligible in early August to sign a contract extension for up to four years and $275 million. He holds a player option for $62 million next season, the final year of a three-year, $175 million deal he signed with the Lakers. The first year of an extension would replace that player option.

 

With extension plans unclear, talks brewed of a potential Davis trade during free agency. The Golden State Warriors were viewed as a potential destination as a way to lure LeBron James to sign with them before he joined the Philadelphia 76ers.

No deal came to fruition, however, and a source told Andscape's Marc J. Spears in late June that the Wizards had no interest in trading Davis and were not listening to offers.

Washington acquired the 10-time All-Star big man in a February trade, following a blockbuster deal for guard Trae Young weeks earlier. Four months after Davis arrived, the Wizards selected AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 pick in the NBA draft. Young and Davis -- with Dybantsa in the long-term -- are part of what Washington hopes will bring a new, successful era of basketball.

The team hasn't reached the playoffs since 2021 and has won less than 20 games in each of the past three seasons.

The Wizards tied Young down with a four-year, $212 million contract during the offseason, but Davis' future still remains up in the air. Young has presumably looked to assist Washington in its efforts. When asked if he talked to Davis about staying with the team, Young said he had conversations with him.

"I ain't on it too much," Young told ESPN with a smile in July. "I think he knows where he wants to be right now."

The All-Star duo are entrusted with not only helping Dybantsa grow, but also other Wizards youngsters like 2025 No. 6 pick Tre Johnson and 2024 No. 2 pick Alex Sarr, too. Davis emphasized that the leadership style he hopes to bring is a simple one: "just helping the young guys."

articles.headline: Anthony Edwards happy to cede PG duties to LaMelo Ball
articles.description: Anthony Edwards says he's happy with the moves Minnesota made over the summer and is excited to continue to develop chemistry with LaMelo Ball.
articles.headlineJa: アンソニー・エドワーズ、ラメロ・ボールへのPG役譲渡を快諾
articles.descriptionJa: アンソニー・エドワーズは、ミネソタが今夏に行った補強に満足しており、ラメロ・ボールとの連携を深めていくことを楽しみにしていると語った。
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- Anthony Edwards reiterated several times how happy he was with the new-look Minnesota Timberwolves roster. And although he said he would miss his long-time teammate Naz Reid, he is already developing chemistry with his new backcourt mate LaMelo Ball.

"I'm going to miss Naz for sure, that's my brother," Edwards said at Wolves media day Monday. "But I'm super happy about the changes in the locker room. Just a bunch of different mentalities, personalities. I think it's going to mesh well together."

After reaching the Western Conference finals in back-to-back years, the Wolves lost in the second round in the 2026 playoffs, prompting a more dramatic shift this summer. The team traded Reid and forward Julius Randle to clear the way to acquire Ball from the Charlotte Hornets, and signed Jonathan Kuminga as a free agent, moves to make the team younger and, they believe, more dynamic.

Edwards said he was excited for the addition of Ball because he it would help him go back to his natural position at shooting guard.

 

"I feel like I'm a natural two guard at heart," Edwards said. "I never thought I could develop any point guard skills. I know [coach Chris Finch] harps on me passing the ball, but now we got LaMelo, so I'm happy."

With Ball playing next to him taking over the ballhandling duties, Edwards said he believed he would have more energy to play defense.

"The last couple years I couldn't play defense as well as I wanted to because I was bringing the ball up," Edwards said. "At times, I had to score all the time. I was super tired, but now I got LaMelo, I got point guards. So, I don't really got to bring it up at all. I can go to the corner for three, four plays in a row and just guard the best players. This year I'm going to be great in my game a lot differently.

Ball spent the first six years of his career in Charlotte before being traded over the summer after one of his strongest seasons. In 72 games, he averaged 20.1 points and 7.1 assists as the Hornets had one of the best records in the league during the second half. Yet, Ball didn't acknowledge feeling surprised by the trade -- "I never really do surprises," he said -- instead, focusing on his budding bond with Edwards.

"Really, we got the same personality," Ball said. "Cool, confident, outgoing. That's my brother and I think we're going to be straight."

Edwards is also coming off one of the best seasons of his young career. He put up a career-high 28.8 points on 48% shooting in 61 games during the regular season, but he was frustrated at times with constant double-teams, especially during the playoffs.

But during his news conference Monday, Edwards was asked about the Wolves having a short window to make their superstar happy.

"Who the superstar?" Edwards asked incredulously. "Me?"

"I didn't know nothing about that. I'm happy."

articles.headline: Evans, Williams, Greenlaw don't have long-term injuries, 49ers say
articles.description: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that injuries sustained by Mike Evans, Trent Williams and Dre Greenlaw on Sunday aren't considered long-term issues.
articles.headlineJa: エヴァンス、ウィリアムズ、グリーンローの負傷は長期化しない見込みと49ersが発表
articles.descriptionJa: 49ersのカイル・シャナハンヘッドコーチは月曜日、日曜日に負傷したマイク・エヴァンス、トレント・ウィリアムズ、ドレイ・グリーンローの怪我について、長期的な問題とはみなされていないと述べた。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers finished Sunday's win over the Arizona Cardinals without receiver Mike Evans (ribs), left tackle Trent Williams (shoulder stinger) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (quad) but they aren't expecting to miss them for long.

Niners coach Kyle Shanahan provided updates on all three injured players Monday, revealing that none of the issues are expected to be long term and that Evans, Williams and Greenlaw will be monitored as this week goes on with the possibility of playing against the Denver Broncos on Sunday not yet ruled out.

"Really, all three of these guys are kind of in the same boat," Shanahan said.

The 49ers also plan to open the practice window for second-year defensive end Mykel Williams on Wednesday. The No. 11 pick in the 2025 NFL draft has been on the physically unable to perform list because of a torn right anterior cruciate ligament. Since he was on the PUP list to open training camp, he's eligible to return to practice now but can't play in a game until Week 5.

On Sunday evening, it was Evans' injury that drew most of San Francisco's concern, in part because it was unclear whether it was a rib or oblique ailment. But Shanahan said Monday that Evans is dealing with a rib issue that the Niners will manage this week, similar to how they did with Evans' hip injury last week.

Evans departed the game against Arizona in the second quarter, walking slowly off the field and favoring his right rib cage before eventually going to the locker room on a cart. The Niners ruled out a potential return for him at halftime.

"We'll have to evaluate him throughout the week," Shanahan said. "It shouldn't be long term and we've got to see how it goes throughout the week."

Trent Williams sustained a stinger in his shoulder and neck area in the third quarter and also went to the locker room on a cart. He soon returned to the sideline but did not reenter the game as Vederian Lowe finished at left tackle.

Shanahan said Trent Williams "should be good to go by Thursday's [practice]," noting that the team will keep an eye out for any issues stemming from the stinger.

Greenlaw left the game late, returned for one play then went to the sideline for good with Shanahan saying after the game that they "shut him down." Shanahan said Monday that Greenlaw has a bruised quad but again indicated that Greenlaw will just have to go easy this week, so the bruise heals.

Elsewhere on the injury report, Shanahan said defensive end Nick Bosa (calf) and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. (ankle) will not play Sunday against the Broncos. Shanahan added that the team is hoping that rookie defensive end Romello Height (broken hand) will return to practice this week after sitting out Sunday's game against Arizona.

articles.headline: Javier Aguirre turned down four coaching offers until 'Valencia called'
articles.description: Former Mexico coach Javier Aguirre said he turned down four other jobs before accepting the challenge to return to LaLiga with Valencia.
articles.headlineJa: ハビエル・アギレ、「バレンシアから電話が来るまで」4つの監督オファーを辞退していた
articles.descriptionJa: 元メキシコ代表監督のハビエル・アギレ氏は、バレンシアでラ・リーガに復帰する挑戦を受け入れる前に、他の4つの監督就任要請を断っていたと語った。
articles.body:
MADRID -- Veteran coach Javier Aguirre said he turned down four other jobs before accepting the challenge to coach struggling Spanish club Valencia, and vowed to regain the fans' support with victories.

Aguirre, taking over his seventh different Spanish club after coaching his native Mexico at the World Cup, was officially presented as Valencia's new manager on Monday.

"I had turned down four other job offers and was happy spending time with my family, but when Valencia CF called, I told my wife we had to come here," the 67-year-old Aguirre said. "She loves football even more than I do, so she was thrilled about it."

Aguirre did not elaborate on the job offers he turned down before agreeing to replace the fired Carlos Corberán.

The 67-year-old Aguirre's third stint as Mexico coach ended with a last-16 loss to England at the World Cup in Estadio Azteca in Mexico City. He previously coached Spanish clubs Osasuna, Atletico Madrid, Real Zaragoza, Espanyol, Leganes and Mallorca.

Aguirre was given a contract until the end of the season, with a club option to extend the deal for an additional year.

Valencia has lost five of its first seven games of the season and is second-to-last in the Spanish league.

Aguirre said he felt welcomed by the fans and sensed a "positive atmosphere" upon arriving at the club, but acknowledged that "it's all about results, and we hope to deliver them as soon as possible."

His first game will be at promoted Racing Santander on Oct. 11.

"People are going to be tired of messages. We're going to play Racing Santander and we're going to go for the win," he said. "The victory is what is needed."

Before Aguirre's arrival, Valencia fans had been protesting against players and team owner Peter Lim, a Singaporean businessperson they say only treats the club as a business.

"The plan is to win, and for the team to have a style and an identity," Aguirre said. "The fans will gradually get on board as the wins start coming."

His hiring completed an early-season reconstruction of Valencia's soccer operations after its poor start in La Liga. When firing Corberán, Valencia also removed chief executive Ron Gourlay and has since appointed Braulio Vázquez as sporting director.

"Beyond his experience, what I liked the most when we started talking was his eagerness to come here," Vázquez said of Aguirre. "We didn't even discuss financial terms. He really conveyed a strong desire to join. I want to thank him and his coaching staff for taking the decision to come to our club during a difficult time."

Valencia hasn't finished higher than ninth in La Liga since coming fourth in 2017-18 and 2018-19. It was ninth last season.
